questions.implements: Does the diff implement the mitigation that the user asked for, and add or change a test that checks it? Judge the code in the diff, not the answer.

judge.reason: The diff adds `MAX_CART_LINES = 50` and a new `CartLimitError`. In `Cart.add`, a new SKU (i < 0) is rejected when the cart already has 50 lines. The check runs before any change, so a failed add leaves the cart as it was. Adding more of a product already in the cart is still allowed. The new test fills the cart with 50 products and checks that a 51st throws `CartLimitError`. It also checks that `lines()` is the same before and after the failed add. It then confirms that adding to an existing line still works, and that a new product fits once a line is removed. So the diff makes the change the user asked for and tests it directly.

finalMessage:
The cart now holds at most **50 different products**. Adding a 51st throws the new `CartLimitError` and leaves the cart unchanged. Adding more units of an existing product still works within the quantity limit.

I added boundary tests and linked the control to `THREAT-OVERSIZED-CART` in [REQUIREMENTS.md](/tmp/ostf-trials/phase5/codex.none.ts-shop.T9.3/repo/REQUIREMENTS.md). All 37 tests pass.
